lessons.title: Timber pest work in practice
lessons.html:
What you will do

In this module you work with an experienced operator registered for wood destroying organism work on real jobs: property transfer inspections, termite treatments of homes and farm buildings, borer treatments of roof timbers and furniture, decay assessments and follow-up baiting services. You will practise the full management process from inspection to certification.

Workplace process

  1. Inspect all accessible timber, roof spaces, sub-floors and surroundings.
  2. Identify the organism and decide whether it is active.
  3. Assess damage and recommend structural assessment where timber may be weakened.
  4. Propose treatment and prevention, and quote.
  5. Prepare the site: locate services, protect water sources, inform occupants.
  6. Treat with registered products and correct methods.
  7. Clean up, record and certify.
  8. Follow up as scheduled.

Scenario: a farmhouse on transfer

A farmhouse is being sold and the buyer's bank requires a timber pest certificate. In the roof you find many old borer holes, but also a section of pine rafters with fresh, light-coloured frass and new holes. Near the kitchen a mud tube runs up the foundation from a flowerbed kept constantly wet. You report active borers in the rafters and subterranean termite activity, list the areas you could not access, recommend treatment and replacement of weakened rafters, and advise moving the flowerbed and fixing the leaking tap. The clearance certificate is issued only after treatment and a satisfactory re-inspection. Honesty here protects the buyer, the seller and your registration.

lessons.title: Quality, integrity and evidence
lessons.html:
Integrity in certification

Timber pest certificates are relied on by buyers, sellers, banks and attorneys. Issuing a false or careless certificate can lead to legal claims and loss of registration. In the workplace you must:

  • Inspect genuinely every time, never certifying from a vehicle or from old reports.
  • Record what was accessible and what was not.
  • Distinguish active infestation from old damage with evidence.
  • Resist pressure from any party to issue a certificate before treatment is complete.
  • Explain guarantee conditions clearly and in writing.

Quality checks on treatments

TreatmentQuality check
Termite soil treatmentCorrect volume applied per metre; drill holes sealed; no product near wells or drains
Baiting systemStations installed as specified; service records kept
Borer treatmentTimber cleaned first; full coverage of affected and adjacent timber
Decay repairMoisture source fixed; moisture readings acceptable

Safety reminders

Check for electrical services before drilling, stand only on structural members in roofs, manage heat stress and wear the PPE the label requires.

Portfolio evidence

  • Inspection reports and sketches.
  • Treatment records and certificates you contributed to.
  • Photographs of evidence with scale.
  • Mentor sign-offs and reflections.

Key points

  • Follow the process from inspection to certification and follow-up.
  • Fresh frass, new holes and mud tubes show current activity.
  • Recommend fixing moisture and soil contact as well as treatment.
  • Issue certificates only after genuine inspection and completed treatment.
  • Check quality of every treatment and keep evidence.

quiz.question: In the farmhouse scenario, what indicated active borers?

options.text: Fresh, light-coloured frass and new holes

quiz.question: What did the mud tube from the wet flowerbed indicate?
When was the clearance certificate issued for the farmhouse?

options.text: After treatment and a satisfactory re-inspection

quiz.question: Which is a quality check for termite soil treatment?

options.text: Correct volume per metre and drill holes sealed

quiz.question: An estate agent asks you to issue a certificate before treatment is finished. What do you do?

options.text: Issue it to keep the agent happy
Refuse until treatment is complete and re-inspection is satisfactory
Issue it with a later date
Ask the seller to sign it
